scope: LONGHORN-48 V2 recurring selector, snapshot/backup retention and credential refusal/recovery integration; not project PASS
conclusions: RecurringJob produces an owned Kubernetes CronJob with Forbid concurrency and OnFailure restart; Pod or Job success alone proves no volume recovery point.

PVC recurring labels override Volume labels only when recurring-job.longhorn.io/source=enabled. StorageClass selectors apply to newly created volumes; product group selection and native source selectors must remain separate assertions.

Normal snapshot/backup jobs skip unchanged data; snapshot qualification changes a separate fsynced file and backup-force-create qualification explicitly forces recovery points. Retention requires real native artifact and backend configuration sets.

Detached recurring work is disabled in this qualified production baseline. Observe at least two completed skipped cycles with unchanged native artifacts and source still detached; do not toggle the setting merely for test convenience.

Reuse unchanged V1 schedule/account/rotation mechanisms through the existing V2-qualified fixture. New evidence must prove source V2 disk placement, credential selection, native failure and independent restore; V1 results do not imply V2 PASS.

Keep both transports available while restoring original credential references and stopping owned schedules, then clean exact business/backup consumers and object-store fixture. Compare original target, foreign schedule/CronJob and detached setting identities after cleanup.
coverage_boundary: These qualifications do not cover enabled detached scheduling, periodic full-backup intervals, SystemRestore, DR or complete LONGHORN-48/final delivery.
